presidential election runoff. Photo by Nelson Almeida/AFP via Getty Images_

Last year, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro [said in an
interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HjGhcK09gJI) that Brazil's next
president would have to commit to pardoning his father, former President Jair
Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest for having attempted a coup d'etat in
2022. And more: When the Supreme Court ruled the pardon unconstitutional, as
it inevitably would, he said that president would have to push it through
regardless, even if it meant interfering in the judiciary with "the use of
force".

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Well, it looks as if this might actually happen: Flavio Bolsonaro himself is
currently the front-runner heading into the presidential runoff on Oct. 25.

The eldest son of Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio became a state congressman in 2003 at
the age of 21, and later won a seat in the Senate. His brothers, Eduardo and
Carlos, are also politicians. Their father entered Brazilian politics in 1989
and served seven terms as a federal congressman, during which, [according to
](https://www.economist.com/leaders/2018/08/11/the-danger-posed-by-jair-
bolsonaro)_[The Economist](https://www.economist.com/leaders/2018/08/11/the-
danger-posed-by-jair-bolsonaro)_ , he was "an obscure congressman whose main
talent was causing offence". The magazine [also called the future
president](https://www.economist.com/the-americas/2017/11/09/jair-bolsonaro-
hopes-to-be-brazils-donald-trump) "anti-gay, pro-gun, and an apologist for
dictators who tortured and killed Brazilians between 1964 and 1985".

Apparently, Flavio is even more nefarious.
